answers.children: Sloughis are moderately good with children. Their reserved nature and independent streak mean interactions stay calm rather than boisterous, yet their large size and sighthound build can make them overwhelming for very young children during sudden movements, while their history of hunting swift game in desert terrain leaves little tolerance for rough play.
answers.other-pets: Sloughis do not always get along with other pets. Strong prey drive from their original role hunting gazelle and hare leads them to chase small animals, and their aloof temperament can create tension with same-sex dogs, though they may coexist peacefully with familiar companions in a calm household.
answers.exercise: Sloughis need at least one hour of exercise daily. Short intense sprints in a securely fenced area suit their unmatched speed and agility as desert sighthounds, and without this release their independent nature surfaces as restlessness, pacing, or fixation on movement outside.
answers.shedding: Yes — Sloughis shed lightly year-round. Their short smooth single coat loses minimal hair compared with longer or double-coated breeds, which keeps the house relatively free of loose fur, yet the sleek texture still produces fine hairs that cling to light fabrics in the home.
answers.hypoallergenic: No breed is truly hypoallergenic, and the Sloughi is not one of those commonly suggested for allergy sufferers. Its short smooth coat still releases dander and fine hair during the light shedding that occurs year-round, so sensitive individuals may react despite the low grooming demands of the breed.
answers.training: Sloughis are not easy to train. Their independent temperament and history of hunting without human direction in North African deserts produce a stubborn streak that resists commands, though their intelligence of 6 allows progress when training respects their reserved and sensitive nature.
answers.lifespan: Sloughis live 12-15 years. Their lean sighthound build and health robustness of 7 support this range, while centuries of adaptation to harsh desert conditions have favoured endurance and quiet dignity over the heavier substance seen in many other large hounds.
answers.size: Sloughis reach 35-50 lb and stand 24-29 in at the shoulder. Their sleek, lightly built frame feels elegant rather than bulky to live with, offering exceptional speed and agility without the heavy substance that would slow them across arid hunting terrain.
answers.barking: Sloughis do not bark much. Bred for silent pursuit of game in open desert, they remain quiet indoors and use their voice sparingly, reflecting the reserved dignity that lets them observe strangers from a distance rather than announce every visitor.
answers.apartment: Sloughis can live in an apartment only with strict management. Their calm indoor presence and low barking score of 2 help, yet the need for daily sprinting space to satisfy their sighthound energy often makes a large securely fenced area more practical than confined living.
answers.first-time: Sloughis are not a good first dog. Their aloofness with strangers, independent decision-making rooted in desert hunting heritage, and difficulty adapting to new environments demand an experienced owner who can meet the specific needs of this reserved North African sighthound without expecting constant affection.
